nothing-happens.title: Start your code
nothing-happens.text: Your code needs a "hat block" on top to tell it when to start. Try "when green flag clicked."

pointers.label: Drag "when green flag clicked" into your code

green-flag.title: Run your project
green-flag.text: Click the green flag above the stage to run your project!

pointers.label: Click this green flag to start!

move-sprite.title: Move a sprite
move-sprite.text: Use "move 10 steps" from the Motion category to make your sprite move!

move-with-keys.title: Keyboard controls
move-with-keys.text: Use "when key pressed" with a "move" block to control your sprite with the keyboard

pointers.label: Drag "when key pressed" into your code

change-xy-position.title: Change x
change-xy-position.text: Use "change x by" for left and right movement

pointers.label: Drag "change x by" into your code

go-to-position.title: Go to a spot
go-to-position.text: Use "go to x y" to put your sprite in a specific place

pointers.label: Drag "go to x: y:" into your code

glide-to-position.title: Smooth movement
glide-to-position.text: Use "glide" instead of "go to" for smooth, animated movement!

add-sound.title: Add a sound
add-sound.text: Go to the Sounds tab to add sounds, then use the "play sound" block

record-sound.title: Record a sound
record-sound.text: In the Sounds tab, click the microphone button to record your own sound!

play-sound-until-done.title: Wait for sound
play-sound-until-done.text: "Play sound until done" waits for the sound to finish before continuing to the next block.

pointers.label: Drag "play sound until done" into your code

say-think.title: Speech bubbles
say-think.text: Use the "say" or "think" blocks to make a speech bubble appear

change-costume.title: Change costume
change-costume.text: Use "next costume" to change how your sprite looks

add-costume.title: Add costumes
add-costume.text: Go to the Costumes tab, then click the cat button at the bottom to add a new costume

animate-costume.title: Animate
animate-costume.text: Put "next costume" inside a "forever" loop with a "wait" block to make a simple animation!

forever-loop.title: Repeat forever
forever-loop.text: Use a "forever" block from Control to make something repeat over and over

repeat-loop.title: Repeat N times
repeat-loop.text: Use "repeat" to do something a specific number of times!

too-fast.title: Slow it down
too-fast.text: Add a "wait" block inside your loop to slow things down

use-variables.title: Make a variable
use-variables.text: Click "Make a Variable" in the Variables category to keep track of things like score!

change-variable.title: Update a variable
change-variable.text: Use "set my variable to 0" at the start, then "change my variable by 1" to update it!

use-lists.title: Use lists
use-lists.text: Click "Make a List" in Variables to store multiple things, like a collection of names!

detect-collision.title: Detect collisions
detect-collision.text: Use "if touching" from Sensing inside a forever loop to detect when sprites bump into each other!

broadcast-message.title: Send messages
broadcast-message.text: Use "broadcast" and "when I receive" to send messages between sprites!

add-sprite.title: Add a sprite
add-sprite.text: Click the cat button below the stage to add a new sprite to your project!

change-backdrop.title: Change backdrop
change-backdrop.text: Click the picture button below the stage to add a backdrop, then use "switch backdrop"!

make-game.title: Make a game
make-game.text: A simple game needs: keyboard controls, something to collect or avoid, and a score variable!

pointers.label: Drag "when key pressed" into your code

clone-sprite.title: Clone sprites
clone-sprite.text: Use "create clone of myself" to make copies of a sprite — great for projectiles or enemies!

pointers.label: Drag "create clone of" into your code

add-extension.title: Add extensions
add-extension.text: Click the blue "Add Extension" button at the bottom-left to get extra blocks like Music or Pen!

no-visible-effect.title: No visible effect
no-visible-effect.text: Some blocks don't have a visible effect on their own — try connecting them to other blocks in a stack!

block-already-there.title: Already there
block-already-there.text: If a block doesn't seem to do anything, the sprite might already be where the block is telling it to go — try changing the number first!

sound-volume-zero.title: Fix volume
sound-volume-zero.text: Can't hear anything? Check if the volume was set to 0 — use "set volume to 100%" to fix it!

sprite-is-hidden.title: Unhide sprite
sprite-is-hidden.text: Can't see your sprite? It might be hidden! Click the "show" eye icon in the sprite info area, or use the "show" block.

sprite-ghost-effect.title: Fix ghost effect
sprite-ghost-effect.text: If your sprite is see-through or invisible, the ghost effect might be on — use "set ghost effect to 0" to make it solid again!

pointers.label: Drag "set ghost effect to 0" from Looks

sprite-too-small.title: Fix size
sprite-too-small.text: Your sprite might be too small to see! Use "set size to 100%" to reset it.

sprite-off-stage.title: Find sprite
sprite-off-stage.text: Sprite missing? It might have moved off the edge of the stage! Use "go to x: 0 y: 0" to bring it back to the center.

pointers.label: Drag "go to x: y:" into your code

stop-project.title: Stop everything
stop-project.text: Click the red stop sign to stop all running scripts — useful when things are going wrong!

debug-with-say.title: Debug with say
debug-with-say.text: Not sure what your code is doing? Add a "say" block to show values while your code runs — it's like X-ray vision for your code!

wrong-sprite-selected.title: Check which sprite
wrong-sprite-selected.text: Code not running? Make sure you added it to the right sprite — click the sprite you want in the sprite pane, then check its code!

pointers.label: Click a sprite to see its code

touching-wrong-color.title: Fix color detection
touching-wrong-color.text: If "touching color" isn't working, make sure you picked the exact right color — use the eyedropper tool on the color square to sample it from the stage!

wait-vs-no-wait.title: Add a wait
wait-vs-no-wait.text: If things happen too fast to see, try adding "wait" blocks between actions — even "wait 0.1 seconds" can help!

where-did-blocks-go.title: Find your blocks
where-did-blocks-go.text: Each sprite has its own code! Click on a sprite in the sprite pane to see its blocks.

pointers.label: Click a sprite to see its code

sprite-has-own-code.title: Separate code
sprite-has-own-code.text: Remember, each sprite has its own separate code, costumes, and sounds — check you're editing the right sprite!

blocks-run-in-order.title: Block order
blocks-run-in-order.text: Blocks in a stack run one at a time, from top to bottom — the order matters!

two-stacks-same-time.title: Do two things at once
two-stacks-same-time.text: You can run two stacks at the same time! Use two "when green flag clicked" blocks to do things in parallel.

pointers.label: Drag "when green flag clicked" into your code

if-not-forever.title: Keep checking
if-not-forever.text: "If" checks only once! Wrap it inside a "forever" loop to keep checking over and over.

deleting-sprite-deletes-code.title: Don't lose code
deleting-sprite-deletes-code.text: Careful — deleting a sprite also deletes all the code, costumes, and sounds inside it!

drag-blocks-to-workspace.title: Start coding
drag-blocks-to-workspace.text: Drag blocks from the block palette on the left into the workspace to start coding!

pointers.label: Drag blocks from here into the workspace

click-block-to-try.title: Try a block
click-block-to-try.text: You can click on any block in the workspace to try it! Click a whole stack to run all of them.

remove-block-from-stack.title: Remove a block
remove-block-from-stack.text: To remove a block from the middle of a stack, drag it out to the side — the blocks above and below will reconnect!

add-event-block.title: Add a hat block
add-event-block.text: Every script needs a "hat block" (the rounded ones) on top to know when to start running.

pointers.label: Drag "when green flag clicked" into your code

batched-updates.title: Why no effect?
batched-updates.text: Blocks that undo each other (like "turn 15" then "turn -15") happen so fast you won't see anything — add a "wait" block between them!

negative-numbers.title: Go backward
negative-numbers.text: Use a minus sign (-) before a number to go backward! For example, "move -10 steps" makes your sprite go the other way.

decimal-numbers.title: Use decimals
decimal-numbers.text: You can use decimal numbers like 0.5! Try "wait 0.5 seconds" for a shorter pause, or "move 0.5 steps" for tiny movements.

greater-less-than.title: Compare numbers
greater-less-than.text: The pointy symbols compare numbers: < means "less than" and > means "greater than" — the open end faces the bigger number!

find-block-by-color.title: Find blocks
find-block-by-color.text: Blocks are color-coded by category! Blue = Motion, Purple = Looks, Pink = Sound, Yellow = Events, Orange = Control.

change-block-menu.title: Change options
change-block-menu.text: See a dropdown on a block? Click it to change the option — like picking a different key, sound, or direction!

insert-reporter.title: Dynamic values
insert-reporter.text: You can drag a round or pointed block into an input on another block to make it dynamic!

right-click-duplicate.title: Duplicate blocks
right-click-duplicate.text: Right-click (or long-press) on a block to duplicate it, add a comment, or get help!

change-xy-explanation.title: Stage coordinates
change-xy-explanation.text: The stage is like a grid: X goes left (-240) to right (240), and Y goes down (-180) to up (180), with center at (0, 0).

understand-seconds.title: Timing tips
understand-seconds.text: 1 second = a quick pause. "Wait 10 seconds" = a long pause. "Wait 0.1 seconds" = super fast! Try different numbers to get the right speed.

custom-blocks.title: Make custom blocks
custom-blocks.text: Click "Make a Block" in My Blocks to create your own custom block — great for cleaning up long scripts!

pen-extension.title: Draw with Pen
pen-extension.text: Add the Pen extension to draw lines and shapes as your sprite moves — try "pen down" + "move" + "turn" in a loop!

music-extension.title: Play music
music-extension.text: Add the Music extension to play drums and instruments — use it in a loop to make a beat!

text-to-speech-extension.title: Sprite talks out loud
text-to-speech-extension.text: Add the Text to Speech extension to make your sprite actually talk out loud!

random-numbers.title: Use random
random-numbers.text: Use "pick random 1 to 10" from Operators to add surprises — great for random positions, sizes, or colors!

ask-and-answer.title: Ask a question
ask-and-answer.text: Use "ask and wait" from Sensing to ask the player a question — their response goes into the "answer" block!

pointers.label: Drag "ask and wait" into your code

touching-color.title: Detect colors
touching-color.text: Use "touching color?" from Sensing — click the color square to pick any color from the stage with the eyedropper!

timer-block.title: Use the timer
timer-block.text: Use the "timer" block from Sensing to time things — combine with "reset timer" to make countdowns or speedruns!

change-size.title: Change size
change-size.text: Use "change size by 10" or "set size to" from Looks to make your sprite grow or shrink!

pointers.label: Drag "change size by" into your code

graphic-effects.title: Visual effects
graphic-effects.text: Try "set color effect" or "set whirl effect" from Looks to add wild visual effects to your sprite!

stamp-block.title: Stamp copies
stamp-block.text: Use "stamp" from the Pen extension to leave a copy of your sprite on the stage — like a trail of footprints!

play-vs-play-until-done.title: Sound timing
play-vs-play-until-done.text: "Start sound" plays and keeps going. "Play sound until done" waits for it to finish. Use "start sound" for background music!

backdrop-events.title: Backdrop triggers
backdrop-events.text: Use "when backdrop switches to" to trigger code when the scene changes — perfect for levels in a game!

pointers.label: Drag "when backdrop switches to" into your code

mouse-pointer.title: Follow mouse
mouse-pointer.text: Use "go to mouse-pointer" or "point towards mouse-pointer" to make sprites follow your mouse!

clone-basics.title: Clone behavior
clone-basics.text: When you create a clone, use "when I start as a clone" to give the clone its own behavior — it's like a copy that can do its own thing!

pointers.label: Drag "when I start as a clone" into your code

show-hide-variable.title: Variable display
show-hide-variable.text: Right-click a variable on the stage to change how it looks — you can make it a slider for testing!

reset-at-start.title: Reset at start
reset-at-start.text: Put "go to x: y:" and "set size to 100" under "when green flag clicked" to reset your sprite at the start!

pointers.label: Drag "go to x: y:" into your code

broadcast-for-levels.title: Game levels
broadcast-for-levels.text: Use "broadcast" to switch between levels or scenes — each sprite can listen for the same message and react differently!

clone-delete.title: Delete clones
clone-delete.text: Don't forget to "delete this clone" when you're done with it — otherwise you might hit the 300 clone limit!

pointers.label: Drag "delete this clone" into your code

repeat-until.title: Repeat until
repeat-until.text: Use "repeat until" to keep doing something until a condition is met — like moving until you reach the edge!

make-story.title: Tell a story
make-story.text: Tell a story! Use "say for 2 seconds", "wait", and "switch backdrop" to create scenes and dialogue.

pointers.label: Drag "say for 2 seconds" into your code

make-animation.title: Make animation
make-animation.text: Create an animation by switching costumes in a loop — draw your own frames in the Costumes tab!

make-music-project.title: Compose music
make-music-project.text: Make a music project! Use the Music extension with "play note" blocks to compose your own song.

make-art.title: Create art
make-art.text: Make art! Use the Pen extension with loops and turns to draw amazing patterns and spirals.

make-quiz.title: Make a quiz
make-quiz.text: Make a quiz! Use "ask and wait" + "if answer =" to check if the player got it right.

pointers.label: Drag "ask and wait" into your code

make-platformer.title: Platformer game
make-platformer.text: Make a platformer game! Use "change y by -2" in a forever loop for gravity, and "if touching color" for the ground.

pointers.label: Drag "change y by" into your code

make-clicker.title: Clicker game
make-clicker.text: Make a clicker game! Use "when this sprite clicked" + "change score by 1" — add costumes to make the sprite react to each click!

pointers.label: Drag "when this sprite clicked" into your code

make-dance-party.title: Dance party
make-dance-party.text: Make a dance party! Add multiple sprites, give each one a forever loop with costume changes and moves, then add music!

make-pet.title: Virtual pet
make-pet.text: Make a virtual pet! Use variables to track hunger, happiness, and energy — and buttons to feed, play, and rest.

surprise-sprite.title: Random surprise
surprise-sprite.text: Try putting "set size to pick random 50 to 200" in your project for fun surprises!

silly-sounds.title: Silly sounds
silly-sounds.text: Try the sound effects in the Sounds tab — there are funny sounds like "boing", "chomp", and "zoop"!

color-changing.title: Rainbow colors
color-changing.text: Put "change color effect by 25" inside a forever loop to make your sprite cycle through rainbow colors!

pointers.label: Drag "change color effect" into your code

spinning.title: Spin around
spinning.text: Put "turn 15 degrees" inside a forever loop to make your sprite spin! Change the number to spin faster or slower.

growing-shrinking.title: Pulse effect
growing-shrinking.text: Make your sprite pulse! Use "change size by 5" and "wait", then "change size by -5" and "wait" in a forever loop.

pointers.label: Drag "change size by" into your code

trail-of-stamps.title: Leave a trail
trail-of-stamps.text: Turn on pen down and move your sprite around with the keyboard — you'll leave a colorful trail everywhere you go!

sound-remix.title: Remix sounds
sound-remix.text: Record your own voice in the Sounds tab, then use "set pitch effect" to make it sound like a chipmunk or a monster!

bouncing-around.title: Bouncing screensaver
bouncing-around.text: Make a screensaver! Use "point in direction pick random 1 to 360", then "forever: move + if on edge bounce"!

pointers.label: Drag "if on edge, bounce" into your code

huge-number.title: Big number issues
huge-number.text: Typed a really huge number? Numbers bigger than about 16 digits lose precision — and really enormous ones get treated as 0!

rotation-style-vs-turn.title: Fix rotation
rotation-style-vs-turn.text: If "turn" doesn't seem to work, check if the rotation style is set to "left-right" or "don't rotate" — change it to "all around" in the sprite info!

pointers.label: Check rotation style in sprite info

costume-center.title: Fix costume center
costume-center.text: If your sprite rotates weirdly, the costume center point might be off — go to the Costumes tab and drag the crosshair to the center of your drawing!

missing-asset.title: Missing asset
missing-asset.text: If a block says a costume or sound name that's grayed out, that asset might be missing — add it back in the Costumes or Sounds tab!

dragging-to-stage.title: Drag to workspace
dragging-to-stage.text: Make sure you're dragging blocks to the code workspace (the big area in the middle), not onto the stage!

tutorial-getting-started.text: Try the "Getting Started" tutorial to learn how to make a sprite move and say hello!

tutorial-getting-started-asl.text: Try the "Getting Started - ASL" tutorial to learn Scratch with American Sign Language!

tutorial-animate-a-name.text: Try the "Animate a Name" tutorial to make letters spin, grow, and change color!

tutorial-animate-a-character.text: Try the "Animate a Character" tutorial to make a character talk, move with arrow keys, and jump!

tutorial-tell-a-story.text: Try the "Create a Story" tutorial to make characters have conversations and switch scenes!

tutorial-say-it-out-loud.text: Try the "Create Animations That Talk" tutorial to use the text-to-speech extension and make sprites speak out loud!

tutorial-imagine.text: Try the "Imagine a World" tutorial to create an interactive world with flying, gliding, and costume changes!

tutorial-add-effects.text: Try the "Add Effects" tutorial to learn about color, fisheye, whirl, pixelate, and other cool effects!

tutorial-make-it-fly.text: Try the "Make it Fly" tutorial to create a flying game with arrow keys, collectibles, and a score!

tutorial-make-music.text: Try the "Make Music" tutorial to pick instruments, create songs, and make a beatbox!

tutorial-pong.text: Try the "Pong Game" tutorial to make a ball bounce off a paddle and keep score!

tutorial-clicker-game.text: Try the "Make a Clicker Game" tutorial to make things pop up, click on them, and keep score!

tutorial-chase-game.text: Try the "Chase Game" tutorial to make a game where you chase things around the screen with arrow keys!

tutorial-video-sensing.text: Try the "Video Sensing" tutorial to use your camera to pet the cat, animate sprites, and pop balloons!

tutorial-face-sensing.text: Try the "Face Sensing" tutorial to put accessories on your face and make games that use face tracking!

tutorial-talking-tales.text: Try the "Talking Tales" tutorial to make characters speak, switch scenes, dance, and ask questions!

tutorial-add-sprite.text: Try the "Add a Sprite" tutorial to learn how to add new characters to your project!

tutorial-add-backdrop.text: Try the "Add a Backdrop" tutorial to learn how to change the background of your project!

tutorial-arrow-keys.text: Try the "Use Arrow Keys" tutorial to learn how to move a sprite around with the keyboard!

tutorial-change-size.text: Try the "Change Size" tutorial to learn how to make sprites grow and shrink!

tutorial-glide-around.text: Try the "Glide Around" tutorial to make your sprite glide smoothly back and forth or to a point!

tutorial-make-it-spin.text: Try the "Make It Spin" tutorial to learn how to make a sprite turn and set its direction!

tutorial-record-a-sound.text: Try the "Record a Sound" tutorial to record your own sounds and use them in your project!

tutorial-hide-and-show.text: Try the "Hide and Show" tutorial to make sprites appear and disappear!

tutorial-animate-a-sprite.text: Try the "Animate a Sprite" tutorial to learn how to switch costumes and create animations!

starter-dance-party.title: Dance Party
starter-dance-party.text: The Dance Party project shows how to make characters dance by switching costumes in a forever loop while the stage plays music!

starter-animate-crab.title: Animate the Crab
starter-animate-crab.text: The Animate the Crab project shows how to bring a character to life with costume expressions, "if on edge bounce," and random positioning!

starter-walk-cycle.title: Walk Cycle
starter-walk-cycle.text: The Walk Cycle project shows how to create a realistic walking animation by combining "move steps" with "next costume" in a repeat loop!

starter-mouse-trail.title: Mouse Trail
starter-mouse-trail.text: The Mouse Trail project shows how to use cloning to create a trail of stars that follows your mouse, with each clone shrinking and disappearing!

starter-food-truck.title: Food Truck Animation
starter-food-truck.text: The Food Truck Animation project shows how to make a scrolling background, spinning tires, and flashing graphic effects with multiple sprites!

starter-make-it-fly.title: Make It Fly
starter-make-it-fly.text: The Make It Fly project shows how to use keyboard sensing and forever loops to make a flying cat dodge scrolling buildings!

starter-maze.title: Maze Starter
starter-maze.text: The Maze Starter project shows how to navigate a ball through a maze using arrow keys and color-touching detection for wall collisions!

starter-dress-up.title: Dress Up Tera
starter-dress-up.text: The Dress Up Tera project shows how to make sprites draggable and use touching detection to create an interactive dress-up game!

starter-pong.title: Pong Starter
starter-pong.text: The Pong Starter project shows how to make a simple game including mouse movement, ball bouncing, collisions, and sound effects!

starter-hide-seek.title: Hide and Seek
starter-hide-seek.text: The Hide and Seek project shows how to make a clicking game with a score variable, random positioning, and show/hide!

starter-stamp-studio.title: Stamp Studio
starter-stamp-studio.text: The Stamp Studio project shows how to use the pen stamp block with if-then conditions to draw colorful patterns that follow your mouse!

starter-parallax.title: Interactive Parallax
starter-parallax.text: The Interactive Parallax project shows how to use math operators and mouse sensing to move layers at different speeds for a depth effect!

starter-soundflower.title: Soundflower
starter-soundflower.text: The Soundflower project shows how to use the loudness sensor and multiply blocks to make a flower that responds to your microphone!

starter-art-alive.title: Make Art Come Alive
starter-art-alive.text: The Make Art Come Alive project shows how to use click events, broadcasts, and glide blocks to animate parts of a painting!

starter-spin-art.title: Spin Art
starter-spin-art.text: The Spin Art project shows how to use slider variables, the stamp block, and move-and-turn to create mesmerizing spiral patterns!

starter-dj.title: DJ Scratch Cat
starter-dj.text: The DJ Scratch Cat project shows how to use key press events and sound blocks to make a DJ mixing board with a looping beat!

starter-piano.title: Piano
starter-piano.text: The Piano project shows how to build a playable instrument with clickable key sprites using the Music extension's play-note block!

starter-fish-pitch.title: Catch the Fish
starter-fish-pitch.text: The Catch the Fish project shows how to use cloning, a score variable, and the pitch effect to make music play higher as you score!

starter-fur-elise.title: Fur Elise
starter-fur-elise.text: The Fur Elise project shows how to use custom My Blocks to organize a song into reusable sections with the Music extension!

starter-drum-sequencer.title: Drum Sequencer
starter-drum-sequencer.text: The Drum Sequencer project shows how to use cloning for a button grid and color-sensing on a moving play head to make a drum machine!

starter-story.title: Story Starter
starter-story.text: The Story Starter project shows how to tell a story with multiple characters using broadcasts to coordinate dialogue and sound!

starter-random-facts.title: Random Facts
starter-random-facts.text: The 5 Random Facts About Me project shows how to create a slideshow presentation using backdrops and key press events!

starter-fill-blanks.title: Fill in the Blanks
starter-fill-blanks.text: The Fill in the Blanks project shows how to make a mad-libs story using ask blocks, variables, and the join operator!

starter-stop-motion.title: Stop Motion
starter-stop-motion.text: The Stop Motion Animation project shows how to create a flipbook-style animation by switching costumes in a forever loop!

starter-adventure.title: Adventure Game
starter-adventure.text: The Adventure with Scratch Cat project shows how to build an interactive adventure with collision detection and broadcast-driven scene changes!

starter-gravity.title: Gravity Example
starter-gravity.text: The Gravity Example project shows how to simulate gravity with velocity variables and conditionals for ground collision!

starter-sound-graph.title: Sound Graph
starter-sound-graph.text: The Sound Graph project shows how to visualize microphone input as a graph using pen blocks, loudness sensing, and math operators!

starter-math-game.title: Math Game
starter-math-game.text: The Math Game project shows how to make a quiz with random number variables, ask blocks for input, and if-else to check answers!

starter-circuit.title: Circuit Simulation
starter-circuit.text: The Simple Circuit Simulation project shows how to use draggable sprites, color-touching detection, and boolean logic to simulate a circuit!

starter-coordinates.title: X and Y Coordinates
starter-coordinates.text: The X and Y Coordinates project shows how the Scratch coordinate system works by letting you drag a sprite and see its position update!

starter-text-speech.title: Text to Speech
starter-text-speech.text: The Text to Speech project shows how to use the Text-to-Speech extension and broadcasts to make characters have a spoken conversation!

starter-pen-flower.title: Pen Flower
starter-pen-flower.text: The Pen Flower project shows how to use nested repeat loops and pen blocks to draw a colorful pattern of rotating squares!

starter-musical-droplets.title: Musical Droplets
starter-musical-droplets.text: The Musical Droplets project shows how to use clones, the Music extension, and math to turn mouse position into musical notes!

starter-translate.title: Translate This!
starter-translate.text: The Translate This! project shows how to use the Translate extension to make characters speak in different languages!

starter-face-filter.title: Face Filter
starter-face-filter.text: The Face Filter project shows how to use the Face Sensing extension to make hats and glasses follow your face in real time!

starter-greeting-card.title: Greeting Card
starter-greeting-card.text: The Greeting Card project shows how to make an interactive card with backdrop switches, glide animations, and sound effects!

starter-quiz.title: Community Quiz
starter-quiz.text: The Community Quiz project shows how to build a quiz with custom blocks, ask-and-wait input, if-else logic, and Text-to-Speech!

starter-trophy.title: Small Wins Trophy
starter-trophy.text: The Small Wins Trophy project shows how to click on sprite parts to cycle through costumes and design a custom award!

starter-kindness.title: Acts of Kindness
starter-kindness.text: The Random Acts of Kindness project shows how to pick a random item from a list using broadcasts and the pick-random operator!

starter-paper-plane.title: Paper Plane Tutorial
starter-paper-plane.text: The Paper Plane Tutorial project shows how to make a step-by-step guide with broadcasts, repeat-until loops, and costume switching!

follow-another-sprite.title: Follow a sprite
follow-another-sprite.text: Use "go to [sprite]" inside a "forever" loop to make one sprite follow another — like a basketball following the cat!

follow-with-offset.title: Follow with offset
follow-with-offset.text: To make a sprite follow below another, use "go to [sprite]" then "change y by -30" — the negative number puts it lower!

pointers.label: Drag "change y by" into your code

bounce-up-down.title: Bounce up & down
bounce-up-down.text: Make a sprite bounce! Use "repeat 10: change y by 5" then "repeat 10: change y by -5" inside a forever loop.

pointers.label: Drag "change y by" into your code

bounce-speed.title: Bounce speed
bounce-speed.text: To change bounce speed, adjust the "repeat" number — fewer repeats = faster bounce, more repeats = slower bounce!

bounce-height.title: Bounce height
bounce-height.text: To change how high the bounce goes, change the number in "change y by" — bigger number = higher bounce!

shoot-at-target.title: Shoot at a target
shoot-at-target.text: Use "glide 0.5 secs to x: y:" to make a sprite fly toward a target — set x and y to where the hoop or goal is!

sprite-hop-jump.title: Make it hop
sprite-hop-jump.text: Press space to hop! Use "change y by 50", "wait 0.3 seconds", then "change y by -50" — that's up, pause, and back down!

pointers.label: Drag "change y by" into your code

sprite-walk-animate.title: Make it walk
sprite-walk-animate.text: To make a sprite walk, use "next costume" with "move 10 steps" inside a forever loop — the costume changes make it look like walking!

sprite-backflip.title: Do a backflip
sprite-backflip.text: Make a sprite do a backflip! Use "change y by 50", then "repeat 10: turn 36 degrees", then "change y by -50" to jump, spin, and land!

sprite-lay-down.title: Lay down
sprite-lay-down.text: Use "point in direction 0" to make a sprite lay down (facing up), or "point in direction 180" to face down — set rotation style to "all around" first!

pointers.label: Drag "point in direction" into your code

crowd-surf-effect.title: Crowd surf
crowd-surf-effect.text: Make a sprite crowd surf! Use "glide 2 secs to x:240 y:50" to slide across, and add "change y by 5" then "change y by -5" in a loop for a bobbing effect!

duplicate-code-to-sprite.title: Copy code to sprite
duplicate-code-to-sprite.text: Yes! Drag your code stack from the workspace onto another sprite's thumbnail in the sprite pane — it copies the whole stack!

pointers.label: Drag code onto a sprite thumbnail to copy it

explore-sprite-abilities.title: What can it do?
explore-sprite-abilities.text: Every sprite can move, change costumes, play sounds, and run code! Click the Costumes tab to see its different looks, and the Sounds tab for its sounds.

pointers.label: Click Costumes to see its looks

access-other-costumes.title: See all costumes
access-other-costumes.text: Click the Costumes tab at the top to see all the costumes your sprite has — you can switch between them with "switch costume to" or "next costume"!

find-sprite-in-library.title: Find a sprite
find-sprite-in-library.text: Click the cat button below the stage to open the sprite library, then use the search bar to find any sprite by name!

add-many-same-sprite.title: Add more copies
add-many-same-sprite.text: To add more copies of a sprite, right-click the sprite in the sprite pane and choose "duplicate" — or add it again from the library! For lots of copies, try cloning.

move-side-to-side.title: Move side to side
move-side-to-side.text: Use "move 5 steps" with "if on edge, bounce" inside a forever loop to make a sprite go back and forth automatically!

pointers.label: Drag "if on edge, bounce" into your code

waddle-side-to-side.title: Waddle effect
waddle-side-to-side.text: Make a sprite waddle! Use "turn right 10" then "wait 0.1" then "turn left 10" then "wait 0.1" inside a forever loop.

fix-upright-rotation.title: Stay upright
fix-upright-rotation.text: Use "point in direction 90" to make your sprite sit upright, or set rotation style to "don't rotate" so it always stays right-side up!

pointers.label: Check rotation style in sprite info

face-without-flip.title: Face left (no flip)
face-without-flip.text: Set rotation style to "left-right" in the sprite info area — then your sprite will mirror horizontally without flipping upside down!

pointers.label: Set rotation style in sprite info

continuous-key-hold.title: Hold key to move
continuous-key-hold.text: Use "forever: if key pressed then change x by 5" instead of "when key pressed" — this way holding the key gives smooth, continuous movement!

wasd-controls.title: WASD controls
wasd-controls.text: For WASD movement, use "forever: if key w pressed, change y by 5 / if key a pressed, change x by -5" and so on for each letter!

sprite-return-to-position.title: Go back to start
sprite-return-to-position.text: Use "go to x: -200 y: 0" to send a sprite back to a specific position — great for resetting enemies or obstacles!

pointers.label: Drag "go to x: y:" into your code

move-multiple-sprites.title: Move both sprites
move-multiple-sprites.text: Each sprite needs its own code! Click a sprite in the sprite pane, then add movement blocks to it — do this for each sprite you want to move.

pointers.label: Click a sprite to add code to it

find-specific-sound.title: Find a sound
find-specific-sound.text: Click the Sounds tab, then click the speaker button to open the sound library — use the search bar to look for sounds like "chirp", "bird", or any sound you want!

insert-audio-file.title: Upload a sound
insert-audio-file.text: To add your own audio file, go to the Sounds tab, hover over the speaker button, and choose "Upload Sound" to pick a file from your computer!

debug-sound-on-collision.title: Fix sound on touch
debug-sound-on-collision.text: If your sound isn't playing when sprites touch, make sure the "if touching" and "play sound" are both inside a "forever" loop — and use "play sound until done" so it doesn't restart every frame!

pointers.label: Drag "play sound until done" into your code

solid-wall-collision.title: Solid walls
solid-wall-collision.text: To stop a sprite from going through walls, use "if touching color [wall color] then move back" — put it in a forever loop so it's always checking!

obstacle-course-game.title: Obstacle course
obstacle-course-game.text: Make an obstacle course! Draw obstacles on the backdrop, then use "if touching color" to detect them. Add keyboard controls and a "go to start" reset!

score-on-event.title: Score points
score-on-event.text: Make a "score" variable, set it to 0 at the start, then use "if touching [sprite]" with "change score by 1" inside a forever loop to score when sprites meet!

countdown-timer-variable.title: Countdown timer
countdown-timer-variable.text: Make a "timer" variable, set it to 30, then use "repeat 30: wait 1 second, change timer by -1" — when it hits 0, stop the game!

color-touch-restart.title: Color = restart
color-touch-restart.text: Use "forever: if touching color [pick a color] then go to x: y:" — this sends your sprite back to the start whenever it touches that color!

kill-brick-game-over.title: Game over trigger
kill-brick-game-over.text: To make a sprite end the game when touched, use "forever: if touching [sprite] then stop all" — you can also broadcast "game over" to show a message first!

ball-bounce-off-sprite.title: Bounce off sprite
ball-bounce-off-sprite.text: To make a ball bounce off a player, use "if touching [player]" inside a forever loop, then "point in direction (pick random)" or "turn 180 degrees" to reverse it!

falling-obstacle.title: Falling obstacles
falling-obstacle.text: To make a sprite fall from the sky, start it at the top with "go to x:0 y:180" then use "forever: change y by -5" to make it fall down!

pointers.label: Drag "change y by" into your code

game-types-overview.title: Game ideas
game-types-overview.text: You can make so many games! Maze games, chase games, platformers, clicker games, pong, quiz games, dodge games, catching games, and more — pick one that sounds fun!

advanced-scratch-examples.title: Amazing Scratch projects
advanced-scratch-examples.text: People have made incredible things in Scratch — 3D engines, full RPG games, music studios, and even working computers! Start with something simple and keep building your skills.

project-idea-suggestion.title: Get an idea
project-idea-suggestion.text: How about making a game where your sprite dodges falling objects? Or an animation of your favorite animal? Or a music machine? Start small — you can always add more!

make-tetris-game.title: Tetris-style game
make-tetris-game.text: Tetris is an advanced project! Start by making one block that falls and stops at the bottom, then add keyboard controls to move it left and right. Build up from there!

pointers.label: Drag "change y by" into your code

volleyball-game.title: Volleyball game
volleyball-game.text: For a volleyball game, make a ball sprite that bounces, two player sprites with keyboard controls, and use "if touching" to make the ball bounce off the players!

pointers.label: Drag "if on edge, bounce" into your code

make-game-more-interesting.title: Improve your game
make-game-more-interesting.text: Try adding: a score variable, sound effects when things happen, a timer, extra levels with backdrops, or power-ups using clones — these all make games more exciting!

scrolling-backdrop.title: Scrolling background
scrolling-backdrop.text: For a continuously moving backdrop, make two copies of the background as sprites. Move both left in a forever loop — when one goes off screen, jump it to the right side!

pointers.label: Drag "change x by" into your code

multiple-backdrops.title: Multiple backdrops
multiple-backdrops.text: Click the backdrop area below the stage and add more backdrops! Use "switch backdrop to" or "next backdrop" blocks to switch between them in your code.

find-sprite-x-position.title: Find X position
find-sprite-x-position.text: Hover over a sprite on the stage to see its x and y position in the sprite info area below, or use the "x position" reporter block from Motion!

other-turn-options.title: Turn options
other-turn-options.text: You can "turn right" or "turn left" by any number of degrees, or use "point in direction" to face a specific way (90=right, -90=left, 0=up, 180=down)!

pointers.label: Drag "point in direction" into your code

forever-block-explained.title: Why use forever?
forever-block-explained.text: Without "forever", your code runs once and stops! The "forever" loop keeps repeating your blocks over and over — that's why your sprite stops moving when you remove it.

no-code-interactions.title: Without code
no-code-interactions.text: You can drag sprites around the stage with your mouse, draw costumes, record sounds, and change the backdrop — all without any code! But code is what makes things interactive.

green-flag-not-moving.title: Nothing moves
green-flag-not-moving.text: If clicking the green flag does nothing, check: do you have a "when green flag clicked" block on top of your code? Is your code connected in a stack? Is it on the right sprite?

pointers.label: Drag "when green flag clicked" into your code

make-sprite-bigger.title: Make it bigger
make-sprite-bigger.text: Use "set size to 200%" from Looks to make your sprite bigger — 100% is normal, higher numbers make it larger!

pointers.label: Drag "set size to" into your code

costume-masking.title: Edit part of costume
costume-masking.text: Scratch doesn't have masking, but you can select just part of a costume to edit! In the Costumes tab, use the select tool to click and drag around the area you want to change.
